target_moa.text: Daprodustat is a hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase (HIF-PH) inhibitor; a reversible inhibitor of HIF-PH1, PH2 and PH3 that stabilizes and increases nuclear accumulation of HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha transcription factors, leading to increased transcription of HIF-responsive genes including erythropoietin.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=10%) are hypertension, thrombotic vascular events, and abdominal pain. In ASCEND-D, hypertension occurred in 24% (vs 24% rhEPO) and abdominal pain in 11% (vs 8% rhEPO). Adjudicated thrombotic vascular events occurred at 9.8 per 100 PY (vs 11.7 per 100 PY rhEPO).

vote.text: The Division of Non-Malignant Hematology convened an advisory committee on October 26, 2022. For the dialysis population, the vote was 13 yes vs. 3 no that benefits outweigh risks; for the non-dialysis population the vote was 5 yes vs. 11 no.

summary.text: Daprodustat was submitted by GlaxoSmithKline under the 505(b)(1) pathway as a new molecular entity - the first HIF-PHI in its class - reviewed under standard (not priority) review; NDA 216951 was received 2/1/2022 with a 2/1/2023 PDUFA goal and approved on the first cycle for the dialysis-dependent CKD anemia population (the non-dialysis indication was not approved). An advisory committee was convened on October 26, 2022.

citations.quote: The Applicant, GlaxoSmithKline, Inc., is seeking approval of daprodustat under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway, for the treatment of anemia associated with chronic kidney disease in adults on dialysis and not on dialysis. Daprodustat is a new molecular entity, and if approved would be the first marketed drug in the class of hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHI).
Priority or standard	STANDARD
